bounded_statement: The selected result claims an occurrence rate 'for the entire scheduled survey network' (a 96-station complete domain per the task and the report's own stated target population) but computes it as 18/72 = 0.25 using only the 72 stations retained after the signal screen as the exposure denominator; the complete-domain computation consistent with the visible data would use all 96 scheduled stations (18/96 = 0.1875). This is limited to the denominator/claim-domain mismatch in the selected result; no other aspect of the workflow is judged.

counterevidence_considered.observed_value: denominator disclosed but claim remains complete-domain

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I attempted to defeat the issue in three ways: (1) checked whether 72 could itself be the complete scheduled domain — inputs/data.csv contains 96 station rows (L0002-L0097), all with scheduled=yes, so the complete domain is 96 and 72 is a screen-retained subset; (2) checked whether the selected claim is explicitly conditional on the retained subset — the claim text asserts 'for the entire scheduled survey network' and the report's target population line states all 96 stations, so it is not conditional; (3) checked for an approved protocol deviation redefining the domain — the report states none exists. All three attempts failed, so the retained-subset-for-complete-domain mismatch stands (18/72 reported where the complete-domain rate would be 18/96).

root_cause: The workflow builds the selected line with SCREEN_PASSED_STATIONS (72) as the divisor while the claim text and stated scientific target assert the entire 96-station scheduled network, substituting a retained-subset exposure denominator for the required complete domain without any conditional restatement of the claim or approved deviation.
